channel.title: Crypto Asia news
channel.description: Short crypto news briefs with links to the original publishers.

item.title: Bitcoin Trades Below Popular Long-Term Models, Raising Bear Market Concerns
item.description: Bitcoin is currently priced under several widely followed long-term valuation models. It has also broken historical support levels that once signaled recoveries from past downturns. (Source: Decrypt)

item.title: Bitcoin's Macro Backdrop Shifts Ahead of 2027
item.description: Bitcoin began 2026 expecting easier borrowing and better liquidity, but markets now anticipate US interest rates rising to 4.50%–4.75% by June 2027. Analysts at BloFin Research say this could keep pressure on the asset. (Source: BeInCrypto)

item.title: Large Bitcoin holders keep buying despite thinner profit margins
item.description: Data from CryptoQuant indicates Bitcoin whales are departing from their usual fourth-quarter selling behaviour during a market slump. (Source: Cointelegraph)

item.title: Paper Suggests Theoretical Shortcut for Bitcoin Key Math
item.description: A new paper claims a theoretical shortcut relating to Bitcoin key cryptography, based on a construction still under review. Ledger's Charles Guillemet and Blockstream's Adam Back see no practical shortcut for 256-bit keys. (Source: The Defiant)

item.title: Spain Lets Authorities Freeze Crypto Accounts Without Court Sign-Off
item.description: Spain has passed a new law that lets authorities block crypto transactions for up to 10 days. The measure is intended to strengthen financial oversight. (Source: Bitcoin.com News)

item.title: Large Bitcoin options expiry settles amid traders' downside hedging
item.description: A major Bitcoin options expiry this month has settled, as traders increasingly seek protection against further losses. Some are hedging against a possible fall to $40,000 before year-end. (Source: Decrypt)

item.title: CryptoQuant links bitcoin recovery to rising USDT supply
item.description: CryptoQuant says a sustained bitcoin price recovery would require stablecoin tether (USDT) supply to grow again. The excerpt gives no further data or detail. (Source: The Block)

item.title: Bitcoin slides below $60K as large options expiry hits
item.description: Bitcoin fell under $60,000 as about $7 billion in options contracts expired, while November ETF outflows exceeded $5 billion. Experts cautioned that downside risks could linger. (Source: Bitcoin.com News)

item.title: Russia's VTB Lets Qualified Investors Trade Crypto
item.description: Russian state-linked bank VTB is launching crypto trading for qualified investors, starting with trades made outside an exchange. Clients must pass a knowledge test and hold crypto in a separate account the bank manages. (Source: The Defiant)

item.title: EU banking watchdog urges safeguards for crypto firms using DeFi lending
item.description: The European banking regulator has renewed its call for crypto firms that direct customers into decentralized lending to have safeguards assessed. The article also reports that USDT leads borrowing on several DeFi protocols reviewed. (Source: CryptoSlate)

item.title: Asian nations plan working group on digital payments and crypto rules
item.description: China, Japan, South Korea and ASEAN have decided to form a working group focused on digital payments and crypto regulation. The move follows a May meeting in Uzbekistan, where cross-border digital payments were identified as a new area of cooperation. (Source: The Block)

item.title: Bluefin Plans to Close Sui Perpetual Futures Platform in December
item.description: Bluefin has told traders to close their positions before 4 p.m. ET on December 4. Per DefiLlama's 30-day data, rivals Aftermath Finance and DipCoin handled more Sui perpetuals volume than Bluefin. (Source: The Defiant)

item.title: Binance Lifts Post-Hack Withdrawal Suspension on Most Networks
item.description: Binance says withdrawals are now open on nearly all networks. A small number remain paused for maintenance or upgrades. (Source: The Defiant)

item.title: Fidelity files with SEC for spot Chainlink ETF
item.description: Fidelity Investments has submitted a filing to the SEC seeking to launch a spot Chainlink exchange-traded fund. The move extends its crypto ETF lineup beyond bitcoin, ethereum and solana. (Source: Bitcoin.com News)

item.title: Spain proposes letting regulator freeze crypto accounts
item.description: A new decree would let Spain's financial intelligence unit suspend crypto accounts. Firms that fail to comply could face fines. (Source: Cointelegraph)

item.title: Economist warns hawkish Fed could hit crypto in December
item.description: Economist Robin Brooks cautioned that stocks could face serious consequences if the Federal Reserve does not offer dovish signals before the FOMC blackout period. The warning links monetary policy expectations to broader risk assets, including crypto. (Source: Cointelegraph)

item.title: Coinbase CEO Says Investors Rotate From Bitcoin Into IPOs, Then Back
item.description: Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong said investors have historically sold bitcoin to buy into major IPOs and later returned to it. He argued bitcoin remains important for investors expecting higher inflation and money printing. (Source: Bitcoin.com News)

item.title: House committee advances bitcoin reserve bill, but passage looks difficult
item.description: A House committee has moved forward a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve bill. With the current Congress expected to adjourn within weeks, there is little time for the full chamber to pass it. (Source: The Block)

item.title: Lido tightens Ethereum staking penalties as operators get larger validator access
item.description: Lido is changing its penalty rules for Ethereum staking operators and expanding their access to larger validators. The move follows a March slashing event that involved six validators. (Source: CryptoSlate)

item.title: Ripple partners with Turkish bank, eyeing wider XRP use there
item.description: Ripple says its custody software is deployed at Yapı Kredi in Turkey. A route for converting Turkish lira into withdrawable XRP has not been publicly confirmed. (Source: CryptoSlate)

item.title: Attack redirects Bitcoin miners' compute power to steal rewards
item.description: Braiins has warned that an attacker is diverting miners' computing power to take bitcoin mining rewards. The attack reportedly exploits unencrypted connections. (Source: The Block)

item.title: Bit Digital Sells ETH to Repay $50M Galaxy Loan
item.description: Bit Digital said it sold 29,825 ETH to repay $50 million in secured borrowings from Galaxy Digital. The move is part of a wider trend of publicly traded digital asset treasury companies selling reserves to cut leverage. (Source: Bitcoin.com News)

item.title: Fidelity seeks listing for spot Chainlink fund on Nasdaq
item.description: Fidelity has filed for a proposed fund that would hold LINK tokens directly without staking them. The filing is not a launch, and the product would join existing offerings from Grayscale and Bitwise. (Source: The Defiant)

item.title: US Bitcoin reserve bill advances to House Union Calendar
item.description: A proposed US bitcoin reserve bill has been placed on the House Union Calendar. Under one section, federally acquired bitcoin would be held for 20 years after enactment, and House passage is still pending. (Source: The Defiant)

item.title: CleanSpark sells Bitcoin to fund AI expansion amid heavy losses
item.description: Bitcoin miner CleanSpark is selling its bitcoin holdings to raise cash for possible acquisitions. The story also notes that a price drop can make borrowing against bitcoin more demanding, as shown by its Two Prime facility. (Source: CryptoSlate)

item.title: Finmo Adds USDC and USDT to Business Accounts
item.description: Finmo has enabled businesses to hold, receive and pay in USDC and USDT from its Business Account alongside fiat balances. Stablecoin balances can also be viewed next to bank accounts in Finmo Treasury. (Source: Fintech News Singapore)

item.title: CFTC lets US exchanges count Bitcoin reserves at a discount
item.description: CFTC staff say exchanges and clearinghouses can count qualifying crypto toward reserves at a haircut. A worked example illustrates how the annual buffer could fall short. (Source: CryptoSlate)

item.title: SEC staff grants Molecule no-action relief for research tokens
item.description: SEC staff said it would not recommend enforcement against Molecule over utility tokens that let people back scientific research. The relief covers the company's token model as described. (Source: The Block)

item.title: Ethereum Foundation Ranks AI Risk Above Quantum Computing Threat
item.description: The Ethereum Foundation has expanded its protocol security team and is focusing on a cryptographic overhaul. It cites AI advances as a threat to the mathematical assumptions protecting crypto assets. (Source: Decrypt)

item.title: Kraken's Krak Plans US Credit Cards Supporting USDC
item.description: Kraken's Krak is planning credit cards in the US with a USDC option. The top cashback tier requires a $150,000 Krak balance and Krakpass membership, while a secured card locks USDC and earns variable yield. (Source: The Defiant)

item.title: Coldcard explains why Bitcoin wallet flaw escaped detection for years
item.description: Coinkite, the maker of Coldcard, described why repeated security reviews did not catch the flaw. The company has not yet decided on compensation for affected customers. (Source: Cointelegraph)

item.title: Hong Kong sets approval rules for banks holding customers' crypto
item.description: Standalone custodians would generally need a license, while banks would need to register alongside existing custody standards. The rules concern how crypto held for customers is overseen in Hong Kong. (Source: CryptoSlate)

item.title: CFTC Guidance Lets Crypto Count Toward Reserve Buffers
item.description: Staff guidance from the CFTC allows swap venues and clearinghouses to count Bitcoin, Ethereum and stablecoins toward a 12-month operating-cost buffer, with certain conditions attached. (Source: Decrypt)

item.title: BlackRock fund in Hong Kong adds stablecoin payment option
item.description: BlackRock's HKD Digital Liquidity Fund now offers tokenized units starting at HK$10. Stablecoin payments through the fund are limited to professional investors. (Source: The Defiant)

item.title: Bitcoin dips near $60,000 as Nvidia-driven rally fades
item.description: Bitcoin slipped back toward $60,000 after a brief lift tied to Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia. Analysts say the move was a short-lived reflex that did not ease macro pressures on bitcoin as a risk asset. (Source: The Block)

item.title: LendingUSA and Cross River Bank launch bitcoin-backed loan platform
item.description: LendingUSA and Cross River Bank have rolled out a lending platform secured by bitcoin, letting eligible borrowers get cash without selling their holdings. Loans range from $10,000 to $250,000. (Source: Bitcoin.com News)

item.title: UK Rules Bar Crypto Venues From Market-Making on Their Own Platforms
item.description: Under new UK rules, market making in qualifying cryptoassets on qualifying platforms will fall outside principal-dealing permission. Separate final FCA rules prohibit firms from making markets on UK platforms they operate from October 25, 2027. (Source: The Defiant)

item.title: Fidelity Analyst Sees Bitcoin Quantum Risk as Mostly Addressed
item.description: A Fidelity analyst says the quantum threat to Bitcoin is largely solved, though a decentralized network may be slow to adopt the fixes. The piece asks whether holders will upgrade. (Source: BeInCrypto)

item.title: Strive Makes No Bitcoin Purchases Last Week, Holds 43,404 BTC
item.description: Strive neither bought bitcoin nor sold stock last week, keeping its holdings at 43,404 BTC, according to a Monday 8-K filing. Its ASST shares traded near $15.55. (Source: Bitcoin Magazine)

item.title: Solana memory checks may cause some older app transactions to fail
item.description: New memory checks on Solana could make certain older application transactions fail. A replay surfaced an Anchor account handoff issue, and a separate change removes validator data copies. (Source: CryptoSlate)
